title: Optimizing CAC Across Distribution Channels
description: Learn to analyze, compare, and optimize customer acquisition costs across different go-to-market channels.

interactions.prompt: Which metric best captures a channel's true cost efficiency for customer acquisition?

options.text: Total marketing spend divided by impressions
Fully loaded CAC including sales, onboarding, and channel fees
Cost per click on paid advertising
Monthly channel subscription or platform fee

interactions.teachingPreamble: Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) varies dramatically by channel—HubSpot reported that inbound channels average $942 CAC in SaaS while outbound averages $1,876. But many teams undercount by excluding onboarding, partner commissions, and sales time. Fully loaded CAC captures all costs to convert a prospect into a paying customer through a given channel.

interactions.prompt: A B2B SaaS company tracks Q3 results: Paid Search CAC $320 (LTV $1,200), Partner Referrals CAC $180 (LTV $2,800), Outbound SDR CAC $750 (LTV $3,500), Content/SEO CAC $95 (LTV $600). Which channel has the best LTV:CAC ratio?

options.text: Paid Search at 3.75x
Partner Referrals at 15.6x
Content/SEO at 6.3x
Outbound SDR at 4.7x

interactions.prompt: Why is blended CAC often misleading when evaluating channel performance?

options.text: It only works for enterprise sales motions
It hides underperforming channels behind efficient ones
It overestimates the cost of organic channels
It doesn't account for annual recurring revenue

interactions.teachingPreamble: Many companies report a single blended CAC—total spend divided by total customers. Shopify's early growth team discovered that breaking CAC by channel revealed their partner/app ecosystem acquired merchants at 1/5th the cost of paid ads. Blended CAC masks this, letting expensive channels hide behind cheap ones, which leads to misallocated budgets.

interactions.prompt: When a channel's marginal CAC starts rising sharply while volume increases only slightly, the channel is likely hitting its ____ ceiling.

options.text: Saturation
Revenue
Conversion
Pricing

interactions.prompt: Your SaaS startup has $200K quarterly budget. Channel A (Google Ads) delivers 400 customers at $250 CAC but is saturating—next $50K would yield only 80 more. Channel B (partner program) delivers 100 customers at $400 CAC but LTV is 3x higher and scaling. Where do you shift the next $50K?

options.text: Keep investing in Google Ads for predictable volume
Shift $50K to partner program for higher LTV returns
Split evenly between both channels
Hold the $50K and test a new third channel

interactions.prompt: What is CAC payback period, and why does it matter more than raw CAC for channel decisions?

options.text: It measures brand awareness ROI over a fiscal year
It shows months to recoup acquisition cost, revealing cash flow impact
It calculates total revenue a customer generates over their lifetime
It tracks the number of touchpoints before conversion

interactions.teachingPreamble: Slack's enterprise channel had a higher raw CAC ($15K+) than self-serve ($200), but enterprise deals paid back in 8 months vs. 14 months for self-serve because of larger contract values. CAC payback period—months of revenue needed to recover acquisition cost—reveals which channels strain or fuel your cash position, which is critical for capital-constrained startups.

interactions.prompt: A Series B fintech is choosing channels for SMB expansion. Rank these from most to least important criteria for channel investment decisions: (a) Lowest raw CAC, (b) Best LTV:CAC ratio with payback under 12 months, (c) Highest volume potential regardless of cost, (d) Strongest channel-market fit for target SMB segment.

options.text: Lowest raw CAC
Best LTV:CAC ratio with payback under 12 months
Highest volume potential regardless of cost
Strongest channel-market fit for target SMB segment

interactions.prompt: Your top partner channel (40% of new customers, $180 CAC, 18x LTV:CAC) just informed you they're launching a competing product in 6 months. What's your best immediate channel strategy move?

options.text: Immediately cut the partner and absorb the volume loss
Accelerate two alternative channels while negotiating transition terms with partner
Ignore the threat since 6 months is a long time
Double investment in the partner channel to lock in customers now

interactions.priorContext: Previously you identified partner referrals as your highest-performing channel with the best LTV:CAC ratio and were scaling investment there. Now that partner is becoming a competitor, creating critical channel concentration risk.
